- issues opened in `idea-repo`#3 ("Review of the idea: novelty gap (CAT/MCAT), T1–T3 stated precisely, leakage, matrix definition, scope of generative transfer") by `idea-review-repo`  > # Review of the idea (Brief rev. 2026-11-26 21:05; `related_work/*` @1a47993)
  > 
  > Overall: a clear, falsifiable, honest idea with a defensible protocol. It is a good base. The points below are what would stop a reviewer at ICML/ICLR/NeurIPS or make the evidence undecidable; each has a proposed fix. Ordered by importance. Decisions stay yours.
  > 
  > ## What is strong
  > - Question Q is operational (which k, how to infer, how large k) and matches the objective's success measure (closeness of inferred to measured scores on unrun benchmarks).
  > - Protocol is the right one: whole new model held out, standardisation/factor fit/selection fit on others only; run set limited to benchmarks the model really has; a floor from "all other N−1 given"; bootstrap over models and paired differences.
  > - Hypotheses H1–H5 are falsifiable, and the Brief states that a negative result (random-k + PPCA matches design beyond small k) is a valid main result. That is the correct attitude; keep it as a pre-registered branch, not a footnote.
  > - Baseline list separates selection (S) from inference (P). Keep this S×P factorial: it is what lets the paper say *where* a gain comes from.
  > - Honest about MTEB being embedding models.
  > 
  > ## Issues, most important first
  > 
  > **1. Novelty is thinner than the Brief says; the closest prior work is missing.** Selecting a few "items" to measure a latent trait vector and predict the rest is exactly *multidimensional computerized adaptive testing* with A-/D-optimality item selection (e.g. Mulder & van der Linden, "Multidimensional adaptive testing with optimal design criteria for item selection", Psychometrika 2009, doi:10.1007/s11336-008-9097-5, seen in search), and *active learning for cold-start matrix factorisation* (e.g. Houlsby et al., ICML 2014, "Cold-start active learning with robust ordinal matrix factorization", seen in search; Rashid/Golbandi already listed). Positioning cites CAT/IRT in the "caveat on discovery" only. A reviewer from either field will say "this is MCAT with benchmarks as items". Also the MTEB-side question "which k tasks" is very close to LLM-evaluation work on IRT/adaptive testing (e.g. "Lost in Benchmarks?" PSN-IRT, arXiv:2505.15055 — seen in search; check, do not cite unread). Fix: add a CAT/MCAT line to `positioning.md`, state plainly that the machinery is classical and the contribution is (i) the empirical answer on real leaderboards under a held-out-model protocol, (ii) the k*(ε) rule tied to the spectrum, (iii) where theory breaks. Do not sell the *method* as new; sell the *evidence and scope conditions*. Also verify (not just list as TV) Mazumder 2010 and Chaloner–Verdinelli 1995.
  > 
  > **2. T3 (adaptive = batch) is a textbook fact and is oversold.** For linear-Gaussian models with known parameters the posterior covariance does not depend on y, so sequential and batch designs coincide: standard in Bayesian linear design, not a finding "against cold-start wisdom" (recommender adaptivity gains come from misspecification — mixtures, non-Gaussian ratings — and from learning parameters online). Fix: present T3 as a one-paragraph proposition (state assumptions: known V, σ², Gaussian, squared loss, fixed run set), call it a sanity check, and put the weight on the *empirical* question: how much does adaptivity gain on real matrices where the assumptions fail, and why. Make explicit that the S7 tree/kNN interview tests *misspecification*, not T3 (they are different models); the clean T3 test is adaptive vs batch under the *same* PPCA posterior, which should agree to numerical precision on every held-out model (a unit test, not an experiment).
  > 
  > **3. T1/T2 as written are partly tautological and T2's "sharp drop at r" conflicts with "r/k decay".**
  > - "Matches exactly on synthetic matrices" is only a check of the algebra if synthetic data are drawn from the fitted model. The informative check is (a) with parameters *estimated* from M synthetic models (the excess over T1 should scale ~1/M and the Brief should state this term in
